candidates.title: Washington opens fresh tariff front across 14 economies
candidates.excerpt: Washington opens fresh tariff front across 14 economies Container shipping faces another bout of trade uncertainty after Washington unveiled plans for fresh tariffs on imports from 14 economies, including several of the world’s largest manufacturing and container export hubs. The Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) on Wednesday published the findings of its investigation into industrial overcapacity, proposing import duties of up to 35%. Vietnam faces the highest proposed rate, followed by India at up to 25% and China and Singapore at up to 20%. The European Union faces a proposed 15% tariff, with similar ceilings for Japan, South Korea and Taiwan. The proposed measures include product exemptions and adjustments for existing duties and trade agreements. Washington specifically identified shipbuilding among the industries benefiting from government policies in China and Vietnam that it claims distort international competition. The proposals have yet to be implemented

candidates.title: ABF market reaches “new equilibrium” after shocks
candidates.excerpt: ABF market reaches “new equilibrium” after shocks The asset-based finance (ABF) market is returning to stability after a period of disruption, with appetite for funding recovering, according to UK consultancy Broadstone. Broadstone’s report, A New Baseline, is based on interviews with senior market participants, including lenders, funders and investors. It found that, after a prolonged period of reassessment, the market has reached “a new equilibrium”, with participants showing renewed confidence and a desire to grow safely. The research identified four trends shaping the market: confidence is returning, due diligence is becoming more demanding, funding is available but selective, and automation presents both opportunities and challenges. candidates.title: Momenta Finance launches working capital facility for UK SMEs
candidates.excerpt: Momenta Finance launches working capital facility for UK SMEs UK business lender Momenta Finance has launched a working capital facility to help small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) bridge gaps in their cash flow. Called Working Capital Finance, the facility offers between £50,000 and £500,000 over terms of up to 12 months, with rates from 1.25 per cent a month plus an arrangement fee. Momenta said the facility is designed to help SMEs buy stock and cover day-to-day running costs. The launch comes as cash flow remains one of the biggest challenges facing UK SMEs, with late payments continuing to tie up cash and hold back growth. In May, the government introduced the Small Business Protections Bill to tackle the problem. candidates.excerpt: MONTREAL — Canadian National will begin increasing passenger train speeds through Repentigny, Quebec, this Friday (Nov. 27) after completing extensive track work at the site of the July 5 derailment in the Montreal suburb. CN said in a statement today (Nov. 25) that it has rebuilt approximately 2,400 feet (750 meters) of track, used more than 2,000 metric tons of crushed stone to reinforce the track foundation, replaced all crossties, and leveled the track. It has also built a new grade crossing and is nearing completion of repairs to a bike path. The 49-car derailment on July 5 caused residents to be evacuated for about five hours while authorities determined that no hazardous materials were spilled [see “CN derailment in Quebec …,” Trains.com, July 6, 2026]. The 172-car train included 13 tank cars containing residue of dangerous goods, according to the Transportation Safety Board of Canada’s preliminary investigation report. candidates.title: Norwood & St. Lawrence locomotive arrives in New York
candidates.excerpt: MADRID, N.Y. — A significant piece of Northern New York’s railroad history has returned home to an enthusiastic community after spending decades in the Steamtown National Historic Site collection. Norwood & St. Lawrence locomotive No. 210 was placed on its new display track at the St. Lawrence Power & Equipment Museum in Madrid on Nov. 20. “I feel elated,” said Roger Austin, the museum’s secretary and a driving force behind the project. “To have it finally come to full fruition is just very satisfying.” Austin worked closely with Steamtown officials to coordinate the transfer of the locomotive, necessary asbestos abatement and wheel repair work, and the truck move from Scranton, Pa., to the Madrid museum. No. 210, an Alco 2-6-0 Mogul, was built in 1923 for the Norwood & St. Lawrence Railroad. candidates.title: News photo: Former Wabash Vista-Dome arrives at Branson Scenic
candidates.excerpt: BRANSON, Mo. — The Branson Scenic Railway has added ex-Wabash Railroad Vista-Dome No. 202 to its fleet, according to a Nov. 23 social media post showcasing the car’s arrival at the Branson Depot. No. 202 was built by the Budd Co. in 1950 for the railroad’s Blue Bird, which ran between St. Louis and Chicago. Prior to relocating to the Branson Scenic, the car had been a regular on Lake State Railway’s office car specials in Michigan. Officials from the tourist railroad expect No. 202 to be ready for passenger excursions in 2027 after some mechanical and interior upgrades. — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire@firecrown.com. candidates.title: TrainsPRO Podcast episode 6 recap
candidates.excerpt: In episode 6 of the TrainsPRO Podcast, Trains Magazine Editor Bill Stephens sits down with intermodal analyst Larry Gross, president and founder of Gross Transportation Consulting. They discuss intermodal’s record year, the growth targets in the proposed Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger, and the threat autonomous trucks pose to rail. Gross has more than 40 years of experience in freight transportation, including 27 years at Wabash National, and writes the monthly Landlines column in the Journal of Commerce. What’s driving intermodal’s record year U.S. intermodal is on pace to top its 2018 record. Gross says it’s important to separate intermodal into its two very different markets. International moves ocean containers inland from ports, while domestic moves mostly 53-foot containers. Overall volume is up 3.4% year to date. US rail traffic rises 7.3% as intermodal gains 10.7% in latest week
candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%.
